headline: A rebound cannot clear the oil, rupee and geopolitical risk-off overhang.
summary: PSX had a rebound session, but the desk remains defensive. The macro regime is risk-off: oil remains elevated, USD/PKR weakened, August inflation rose to 11.1%, and the SBP held 11.5%. E&P offers the clearest relative support, while selective banks and a few quality names can stay on the screen; OMCs, cement and leveraged cyclicals remain exposed. Fresh dashboard signals are low confidence, so this is a patient watchlist for confirmation, not a broad risk-on read.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Elevated oil supports E&P relative to the wider market, although the same shock raises import-bill and inflation risk.

sectors.name: Selective banks
sectors.why: The SBP rate hold and stronger banking resilience help visibility, but risk-off flows and moving-average weakness require selectivity.

sectors.name: Fertilizers
sectors.why: EFERT has a constructive trend and improving forward view, but its high payout leaves less room for an earnings disappointment.

sectors.name: OMCs and refineries
sectors.why: Fresh fuel-price increases and elevated crude keep margin timing and working-capital risk high.

sectors.name: Cement and leveraged cyclicals
sectors.why: Fuel costs, tight financial conditions and weak risk appetite still weigh on broad cyclicals.

watchlist.angle: The dashboard's current stoch_double_bottom signal is a proven strategy_map setup. Fundamentals are mixed but cheap with healthy profitability, and the 2026-09-11 FY26 profit surge is the dated catalyst.
watchlist.risk: The stock remains below SMA20, is small-cap with thinner liquidity, and a failed rebound would weaken the oversold setup.

watchlist.angle: The dashboard's current oversold_bounce signal is paired with an attractive fundamental rating: cheap valuation, an improving forward view, healthy profitability and a covered dividend. Entry into the KSE-30 on 2026-09-15 is the dated index catalyst.
watchlist.risk: The stock remains below SMA20 and SMA50, so the recovery setup is still inside a selective bank tape.

watchlist.angle: The dashboard's current triple_ema_align signal has trend support: quant places MTL above SMA20 and SMA50 and at a 20-day high. Fundamentals are mixed because valuation is expensive and payout is stretched; the 2026-09-16 results date is an unconfirmed calendar estimate.
watchlist.risk: A disappointing result or a reversal below the moving averages would expose the valuation and dividend-sustainability weak points.

watchlist.angle: The dashboard's current stoch_bull_trend signal is paired with a mixed-but-cheap fundamental rating. The 2026-10-22 book-closure date is confirmed in the calendar, while quant shows a sharp one-day rebound that still sits below SMA20.
watchlist.risk: Small-cap liquidity, a higher beta and the gap below SMA20 leave the rebound vulnerable if participation fades.

watchlist.angle: OGDC is the relative E&P hedge to monitor: strategy_map lists a proven lowvol_pullback setup, fundamentals are attractive with strong profitability, and the 2026-09-15 oil-supply report is a dated sector catalyst. The dashboard has no current OGDC trigger.
watchlist.risk: Quant still places OGDC below SMA20 and SMA50, while a further oil-driven macro shock could hurt the broader tape even if E&P holds up relatively.

catalysts.event: Oil-supply concerns and a domestic fuel-price increase kept the energy and inflation channel active.
KSE-30 recomposition took effect, with BAFL entering the index.
Scheduled SBP release deadline for August 2026 balance-of-payments data; MTL's estimated results date is unconfirmed.

risks: Further Middle East escalation could lift oil again and deepen the import-bill shock.
Fuel-price increases and USD/PKR pressure could keep inflation expectations sticky and financial conditions tight.
The rebound could fail if low-confidence signals lose support; small-cap liquidity and unconfirmed calendar estimates add execution and event risk.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
